hypotheses.statement: There are a positive integer $q$ and a $C^1$ self-map $f$ of the compact smooth manifold $$M=(\mathbb R/100\mathbb Z)\times(S^2)^{q+1}$$ such that $h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)=0$ and $f_*:H_2(M;\mathbb R)\to H_2(M;\mathbb R)$ has eigenvalue $2$. In particular, $$h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)=0<\log 2\le \log\rho(f_*).$$

For the choices above, with $q$ finite and $L>\max\{B,2\}$, the series [eq:input] defines $C^1$ maps $U_\ell\colon(\mathbb R/100\mathbb Z)\times\Sigma\to\mathbb C$. Consequently, [eq:map] defines a $C^1$ self-map of the nonempty compact smooth manifold $M$.

For the map $f:M\to M$ constructed in Section 2, every $x\in M$ satisfies $$\operatorname{dist}\bigl(f^n(x),Z_0\cup Z_\infty\bigr)\longrightarrow0 \qquad(n\longrightarrow\infty)$$ in every compatible metric on $M$. More precisely, if the lifted clock of the orbit is bounded above, then the clock converges to $50$ modulo $100$ and $z_n\to0$. If that lift is unbounded above, then $z_n\to\infty$ in $\Sigma$ and all registers are identically zero from some time onward.
If $(t_n)$ is bounded above, then $t_n\to50+100k$ for some integer $k$ and $z_n\to0$. No condition on the initial register values is required.

In every complete passage as above, all registers are reset to zero before the first index in $I$. The set $I$ is nonempty, has at most five elements, and contains an index $i$ with $\alpha(s_i)=1$. For every $i\in I$, $$\label{eq:preparation-radius}
 |z_i|>\tfrac12.$$ There also exists an index $j$ in this passage with $s_j\in[76,77]$ and $\beta_\ell(s_j)=1$ for at least one $\ell$.

Let $F:X\to X$ be a continuous map of a nonempty compact metric space $(X,d)$, and let $Z\subseteq X$ be a nonempty compact set with $F(Z)\subseteq Z$. Suppose that $$h_{\mathrm{top}}(F|_Z)=0
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  d(F^n x,Z)\longrightarrow 0
  \quad\text{for every }x\in X.$$ Then $h_{\mathrm{top}}(F)=0$.

Let $\Sigma=\mathbb C\cup\{\infty\}$ be the sphere, let $A>0$, and write $D_A=\{v\in\mathbb C:|v|\leq A\}$. Suppose that a continuous map $T:\Sigma\to D_A$ satisfies $$T(re^{i\theta})=R(r)e^{i\theta}
  \qquad(0\leq r\leq A),$$ where $R:[0,A]\to[0,A]$ is continuous and nondecreasing, with $R(0)=0$. Then the coordinatewise map $T^{\times q}:\Sigma^q\to\Sigma^q$ has zero topological entropy for every integer $q\geq1$.
The map $f$ defined in [eq:map] has $h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)=0$.
For the map $f$ in [eq:map], the action $f_*:H_2(M;\mathbb R)\to H_2(M;\mathbb R)$ has eigenvalue $2$.
